analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the indexed threat model and selected T-041 details. No independently supported regression is established in this scope. ProviderLoop+ModelSwitch.swift:46 adds a transition generation before awaiting the actor-owned switch task; existing ownership, cancellation, memory admission and coordinator drain/readiness checks remain unchanged. Generation consumers must be checked in integration for stale-result rejection and lifecycle availability.
ProviderLoop+Prefetch.swift:50-56 now routes consented, nonordinary builds to handleAutopilotDownloadRequest before the ordinary eligibility, shutdown and drain guards (62-84). This is an observed delegation, not proof those controls are absent: integration must inspect that handler for equivalent capability/lifecycle checks, bounded disk/download admission, verification and prevention of ordinary-serving promotion. At :353, autopilotSetAllows replaces settings-based successor permission; its semantics and control invalidation need reconciliation with the new inventory behavior.
ProviderLoop+PrefetchPublication.swift patch head :25 exposes the unchanged failed-self-test predicate internally, :48 adds advertisement occurrence tracking, and :261-265 allows verified builds to join inventory through joinsAutopilotSetWhenVerified. Integration must inspect those helpers, publication guards and consumers to ensure consent, hashes/self-test refusal, selection generations and serving leases remain authoritative. Relevant contracts are A-004, TB-002/TB-007, T-012/T-027 and TB-011/T-052/T-053; inventory inclusion must not become serving authorization. The coordinator is trusted, so coordinator requests alone do not establish an attacker trigger.
No supplied changes directly modify prompt encryption, credentials, Apple proofs, billing, fan authority or T-041 cache crypto/account scoping. Missing helper implementations and bounded publication context are coverage limits, not assurances of safety; resolve these PR-related cross-file questions in the integration pass.
